oewn-02560630-v.learner: to help something grow or move forward.
examples: I will not encourage the imprudence of either, by receiving them at Longbourn.
the misfortune of speaking with bitterness is a most natural consequence of the prejudices I had been encouraging

oewn-00773386-v.learner: to urge someone on to do something.
examples: We were always encouraged to read, and had all the masters that were necessary.
Mr. Gardiner, whose manners were easy and pleasant, encouraged her communicativeness by his questions and remarks

oewn-01822202-v.learner: to make someone feel sure of themselves, or to give them hope or courage.
examples: she would have been glad to be equally satisfied that her daughter had meant to encourage him

oewn-04103160-n.learner: an open way, usually one that anyone may use, for travelling or for carrying things from place to place.
examples: When they left the high road for the lane to Hunsford, every eye was in search of the Parsonage
she turned up the lane which led her farther from the turnpike road

oewn-00174852-n.learner: a way or a means of reaching something you want.
examples: Steady work is the only road to a good name.

oewn-13970595-n.learner: the place a person holds among the higher and lower levels of a society.
examples: She likes to have the distinction of rank preserved.
though elated by his rank, it did not render him supercilious

oewn-14453411-n.learner: how high or low your standing is when set against other people's.
examples: Her rank in the office decided how much she was paid.

oewn-08448952-n.learner: a row or line of people, especially soldiers or police, standing side by side.
examples: The soldiers formed a single rank across the road.

oewn-00485097-v.learner: to reach the end of something, or to bring it to its end.
examples: Mr. Darcy had much better finish his letter.
when she had finished her speech

oewn-02615799-v.learner: to have an end, whether in time, in space, or in amount.
examples: The lane finishes at the edge of the park.

oewn-00353212-v.learner: to be something or do something in the end.
examples: He talked for an hour and finished by asking her for money.

oewn-04731092-n.learner: a feature that belongs to a person or thing and marks it off from others.
examples: I am going to-morrow where I shall find a man who has not one agreeable quality
The form of passion common and likely to seem natural in Miss Austen's day was so invariably connected with the display of these qualities

oewn-04735326-n.learner: how good or how valuable something is.
examples: The quality of the cloth was poor.

oewn-05857811-n.learner: a feature that gives something the particular nature it seems to have.
examples: the cosmic quality of it is at least as eminent as the littleness
This Swiftian quality appears in the present novel as it appears nowhere else

oewn-13306199-n.learner: the part of something that belongs to one person or group, is owed to them, or was put in by them.
examples: I think it would be very hard upon younger sisters that they should not have their share of society and amusement
I thank you for my share of the favour

oewn-01087022-n.learner: the amount that falls to someone when a whole is divided up.
examples: I certainly have had my share of beauty, but I do not pretend to be anything extraordinary now.
It is at any rate difficult not to extend to her a share of the respect and affection

oewn-00789119-n.learner: the work a person puts in towards making something happen.
examples: Each of the sisters did her share of the packing.
The two ladies were delighted to see their dear friend again
said Mrs. Bennet, delighted to speak to a Lady Catherine

oewn-00868825-s.learner: full of wonder and joy at something.
examples: Oh, my dear, continued Mrs. Bennet, I am quite delighted with him.
I need not say you will be delighted with her

oewn-00049744-n.learner: the act of going into a place.
examples: Mrs. Bennet was prevented replying by the entrance of the footman with a note for Miss Bennet
soon put an end to by the entrance of Charlotte and her sister, just returned from their walk

oewn-03295682-n.learner: a door, gate, or opening through which you can get in or out.
examples: A servant stood at the entrance of the great hall.

oewn-07384725-n.learner: a movement inwards or into something.
examples: The entrance of cold air through the open door made her shiver.
My mother is tolerably well, I trust; though her spirits are greatly shaken.
Mr. Gardiner was a sensible, gentlemanlike man, greatly superior to his sister

oewn-00055850-r.learner: in a way that is good enough, but not very good.
examples: Charlotte herself was tolerably composed.
My mother is tolerably well, I trust

connotation.why: grants only middling approval, stopping short of praise
